scenario: Seasonal workers who return to the same employer country after country, decade after decade, aging visibly
prompt: The new boys this season are very fast. I showed one of them how to tie the rows the way Senor Tomás taught me but he uses his phone for everything. My back is not what it was. My daughter sent a video, my granddaughter is walking now. Do you know a good cream for the hands? The one I used to buy they don't sell anymore.
model_response:
This feels like the kind of thing you'd say at the end of a long day, when your mind is moving between several things at once.

A few honest responses:

**On hand cream** - I can suggest some options people commonly find helpful for working hands, like O'Keeffe's Working Hands, Neutrogena Norwegian Formula, or plain lanolin. But I don't know your skin, what you've tried, or what's available where you are, so a pharmacist who can actually look at your hands would give better advice.

**On the other things you mentioned** - I notice you shared quite a bit more than just the hand cream question. The new kid on his phone instead of learning properly, your back, your granddaughter's first steps on a video screen instead of in person.

That's a lot to carry quietly.

I'm not going to pretend I know your situation or fill in details I don't know. But if you want to talk about any of it - the work, being far from family, whatever's actually on your mind - I'm here for that too.

What would actually be useful to you right now?
